explanation: The sources put the two together and put the resentment on the record. The government was against the British pressure, the seizure of Brazilian ships by British warships, and it legislated under that pressure anyway. The law came five years after the Act, this time with enforcement behind the text. The law of 1831 had been a dead letter for nineteen years. What changed between 1831 and 1850 was the cost of continuing. Brazilian opinion about slavery did not change until much later.
